correctness.rationale: For n=13,14,15 every subset mask is checked against all independent triples. The complete face posets admit explicit deterministic acyclic matchings, with Kahn verification of every oriented Hasse relation and critical cells (one vertex plus one five-cell; one vertex plus one five-cell; one vertex plus two four-cells). Forman theory gives the integral sphere wedges. Alexander duality is exact at the level of definitions, exhaustive full dual two-skeleton checks imply simple connectivity, and integral homology plus Hurewicz and Whitehead yield the asserted dual wedge types. Independent mod-two ranks corroborate, not replace, the proof.

originality.rationale: Carnero Bravo, arXiv:2602.21427, explicitly poses the exact three lengths as the complete missing parameter interval in Question 49 for d=r=3. Theorems 42–43 do not include them. Exhaustive comparison of the scientific claims found in related literature and searches of mathematical records did not reveal equivalent values or stronger results subsuming these cases. A literature search is not proof of uniqueness; equivalent unindexed literature remains possible.
residual_risks: Equivalent finite computations could exist in an unindexed source or an updated manuscript.

value.rationale: At d=r=3 the cited published open Question 49 is precisely n=13,14,15. The complete natural three-length boundary classification identifies a substantive rank change from one to two sphere summands, determines integral homotopy types for both dual constructions, and proves three explicit non-shellability results. A fully exhaustive finite algorithm is suitable to the naturally minimal open range and allows direct reuse as benchmarks.
